verses.1: And it came to pass that Jonathan, son of Saul, said to the young man who carried his armor: “Let us go to the camp of the Philistines. But do not tell his father anything about this.”
verses.2: And Shaul sat at the end of the valley, under the hill that was in Migron. And the people who were with him numbered about six thousand men.
verses.3: And Ahia, son of Ahithub; Ahia, son of Icches; and Eliezer, son of Pinehas, were priests. Jehovah carried them away in his glory. The people did not know that Jonathan had gone away.
verses.4: And among those who were to be carried away, Yonatan wanted to carry them away from the state of Philistines. One of them was called “Shen-Ha-Selah”, and the other one was called “Shen-Ha-Selah”.
verses.5: One of the horns is pointing upward from the side, while the other is pointing downward from the back.
verses.6: And Jonathan said to the boy, “Carry all these things with you. Let us go to those places where people are suffering. May Jehovah do whatever He wants to do for us. After all, Jehovah has no limit in His power to save people, whether in large numbers or in small numbers.”
verses.7: And he said to him, “Do whatever is in your heart. I am with you, just as your heart desires.”
verses.8: And Jonathan said, “Look, we are going over to those people, and we will be revealed to them.”
verses.9: If they say to us, “Come to us until we reach you,” then we will stand beneath them, but we will not go up to them.
verses.10: And if they say, “Come upon us and overpower us!” Then let God give them defeat in our hands. That will be our victory.
verses.11: And they both went out to the Philistine camp. They said to the Philists, “Look! These foreigners are coming from the wilderness.”
verses.12: And the people of the camp answered Yonatan and his followers, saying, “Come to us, and we will tell you something.” Yonatan said to his followers, “Come after me. For Jehovah has given these things into the hands of Israel.”
verses.13: Yonatan climbed up on his hands and feet. He carried all his possessions with him. Then they fell down before Yonatan. His companions then carried his dead body away.
verses.14: And the first strike was made by Jonathan. He struck with such force that twenty men were killed. It was like half of the entire army being destroyed.
verses.15: There was fear in the camp in the field, and among all the people who were in a state of distress and destruction. Even those who were healthy and strong also felt afraid. The earth became a place of terror, and it became a time of God’s wrath.
verses.16: And the Zophim saw Shaul in the land of Benyamin. And behold, the man was dead. Then he went away and disappeared.
verses.17: And Shaul said to the people who were with him, “Please look at who has left us. There is no Yonatan anymore; all of them have been taken away.”
verses.18: And Shaul said to his brother Ahija, “The ark of the Lord was there on that day, along with the Israelites.”
verses.19: And it happened that Shaul spoke to the priest and to the leaders who were in the camp of the Philistines. Then Shaul went and said to them, “Your hands are gathered.”
verses.20: Shaul and all the people with him cried out in despair. They rushed into the battle. And there they saw that one man had been killed by another man, in a very tragic manner.
verses.21: And the foreigners became part of the Philistines, just as they had done before. They came with Shulhan and Yonatan to join Israel.
verses.22: And all the Israelites who were trapped in Mount Ebal heard that the Philistines had done a miracle. So they also joined their hands in battle.
verses.23: And the LORD saved Israel on that day. The battle passed through the house of Awn.
verses.24: And on that day, an Israelite man went forth and told the people, “Look! There’s a man who eats bread until morning. I will avenge my brother’s injury. Then no one in the land will be able to eat bread anymore.”
verses.25: And all the land came into the forest, and the ground became covered with grass in front of the fields.
verses.26: And the people went into the forest. There, they saw that the serpent was moving forward, but its hands couldn’t reach its mouth. The people were afraid of the serpent.
verses.27: And Jonathan did not hear his father’s command at the seventh hour. He then threw off the end of his staff into the bushes. His eyes were filled with tears.
verses.28: And one man from the people said, “Shibei, your father has taken the people away. He said, ‘Today, this man will eat bread.’ And the people became afraid.”
verses.29: And Jonathan said, “My father has ruined this land. Please see that my eyes have indeed seen it clearly; I have indeed tasted the bitterness of this land.”
verses.30: Even though I ate today, the people suffered greatly because they found that at this time, there was no more food in the Philistines’ lands.
verses.31: And on that day, the Philistines attacked from Micmasch Ayalona. The people were terrified.
verses.32: And the people went into the fields. They took sheep, goats, and lambs. They slaughtered them, and the people ate the meat.
verses.33: And they said to Shaul, “Look! The people have sinned against God by eating meat that has been slaughtered in blood.” He replied, “In your clothes, then, let us build a great altar today.”
verses.34: Shaul said, “Let the people come forward. Tell them that they must bring before me a man who is lame and a man who has a broken leg. Then they shall slaughter him there, and eat his flesh. But they must not sin against God by eating meat that has been slaughtered in this way.” Then all the people brought forward a man who was lame at night. They slaughtered him there.
verses.35: And Shaul built an altar for Jehovah. From that moment on, he began to build altars for Jehovah as well.
verses.36: And Shaul said, “Let us go after the Philistines at night. We will attack them until dawn. No one will remain with them.” They said, “Do whatever you want.” Then the priest said, “Let us go now to God.”
verses.37: Shaul asked God, “Have you sent them into the hands of Israel?” But God did not answer him that day.
verses.38: And Shaul said, “Let the people see all these things. Let them know and see how great this sin was today.”
verses.39: For Jehovah, the Savior of Israel, will surely be with us in our days. He will not leave us; no one can oppose Him among all the people.
verses.40: And he said to all of Israel, “You will be one tribe, and I and Jonathan my son will be one tribe.” The people said to Shaul, “Do what is right in your eyes.”
verses.41: And Shaul said to the LORD, “Lord of Israel, make them pure.” Then Jonathan and Shaul were captured, and the people also went away.
verses.42: And Shaul said, “Let them be separated from me and from Jonathan, my son.” So Jonathan was taken away.
verses.43: And Shaul said to Jonathan, “Tell me what you have done.” Jonathan replied, “I have done what I should have done at the end of the path that I was on. What I have done is true.”
verses.44: And Shaul said, “This is what God will do. And just as Jonathan died, so too will he be resurrected.”
verses.45: And the people said to Shaul, “Yonatan died because of the great deeds he did for Israel. May the Lord have mercy on him! If his head were crushed by the ground, it would be like a people who do God’s work. But today, the people saved Yonatan from death.”
verses.46: And Shaul went up from behind Philistines. And the Philistines went to their place.
verses.47: And Shaul ruled over Israel. He fought against all his enemies, including Moab, Benjamin, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. He fought against everyone who opposed the Jews.
verses.48: And he made Hail and Yakhk; and he rescued Israel from the hands of Sheshukh.
verses.49: And the sons of Shaul were Yonatan, Ishvi, and Malchishu. The names of his two daughters were Bakira Merav and Khetana Mikhallah.
verses.50: And the name of Shemuel’s wife was Ahinoam, daughter of Ahituphchag. And the name of his chief priest was Abinadab, son of Nar, son of Shaul.
verses.51: And Kish, son of Shaul; and Ner, son of Abiner, son of Aviel.
verses.52: And the war against the Philistines continued for all of Shaul’s days. Shaul saw that every powerful man and every warrior was gathered together against him.
